beats.text: $\text{Erd\H{o}s}$ (1974): can a big set avoid every copy of $\{1/2, 1/4, \dots\}$?
Schematic: $E$ fills most of $[0,1]$, with small gaps from a random routing tree
Shift and scale the sequence anywhere: one of its points lands in a gap

steps: Carve small gaps at random, steered by a tree of coin-flip tables
Each copy needs only a few scales checked, so a union bound works
With positive probability, every copy lands a point in a gap

sources.quote: Erdős asked in 1974 whether every infinite set $A$ can be "avoided"
Even $A = \lbrace 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, \dots\rbrace$ was open for fifty years
The set depends on $q$, and the full conjecture for all infinite sets is untouched.
